_doc: Category 17 (Pet Foods) compiler config for compile-cat17.mjs. THE KEY DECISION: pet food is legally FEED (EU Directive 2002/32, FDA CVM guidance, AAFCO model regulations, Japan's enforced pet-food maxima, China's draft pet-food guidance), whose heavy-metal limits are generally LAXER than human food. HMTc deliberately overrides the feed floor and certifies each (subcategory, analyte) to the strictest applicable HUMAN-FOOD sovereign maximum for the nearest human-food analog, as a voluntary over-compliance. Every value is therefore a `read_across` with human_grade:true — never a `gov` cell, because no government sets this maximum for a pet product. The applicable feed-law floor is looked up from the register and disclosed on every cell (feed_floor) so the derivation states honestly: feed law permits X; HMTc certifies pets to the stricter human-food limit Y. Basis is never conflated: dry (as_sold) products read across only from dry human analogs; wet (as_consumed) products only from as_consumed analogs; no wet/dry conversion is performed.
feed_law_note: Pet food is legally governed by feed law — EU Directive 2002/32/EC on undesirable substances in animal feed, FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine guidance, and AAFCO model regulations — whose maximum levels are generally laxer than the corresponding human-food limits. Japan (FAMIC pet-food standard) and China (draft pet-food guidance) set enforced or proposed pet-food maxima in the same lax range. The HMTc standard for each analyte is not the feed limit: it is the strictest applicable human-food sovereign maximum for the nearest human-food analog, adopted as a voluntary human-grade over-compliance. The feed floor is disclosed on every row and never selects the number.

dry-plant-composite.analog_label: the plant-carbohydrate fraction of a complete diet — cereals, grains, pulses, and starchy tubers (adult/general human food, as sold)

iAs.control: Where no human-food inorganic-arsenic maximum applies to the plant fraction, total arsenic is measured on every lot and bounds the inorganic fraction; an elevated total-arsenic result triggers arsenic speciation. Inorganic arsenic in rice-inclusive diets is limited numerically by the rice read-across where it applies.
iAs.reference_method: Total As by ICP-MS; inorganic As by HPLC-ICP-MS (EN 16802 or equivalent) on an elevated total-As result.

tHg.control: Mercury does not accumulate materially in terrestrial cereal, pulse, or tuber crops; no general human-food cereal mercury maximum binds this fraction below the disclosed read-across. Total mercury is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control.
tHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 (thermal decomposition/amalgamation AAS) or ICP-MS.

Cr.control: No government sets a total-chromium maximum for general cereal, pulse, or tuber human foods; total chromium is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control and gates the Cr(VI) reflex.

Ni.control: Where no human-food nickel maximum applies to the plant fraction, total nickel is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control. Nickel in cereals and pulses is limited numerically by the EU cereal nickel read-across where it applies.

Al.control: No government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for general (non-infant) human foods; aluminium is a ubiquitous crustal element with no established food maximum for adult foods, and the only human-food aluminium numbers on the books are permitted food-additive residue limits (e.g. alum firming agents), which are not contaminant maxima. Aluminium is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control rather than limited to a number no sovereign sets as a contaminant ceiling.
Al.reference_method: Total Al by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion.

Sn.control: Tin is a can-migration analyte: it enters food by dissolution from tin-coated can walls. Dry, non-tinplate pet food (kibble, semi-moist, freeze-dried, treats, chews) has no tin source. Every human-food tin maximum is scoped to canned/tin-coated product; a canned pet product is certified under the canned-wet tin read-across instead.
Sn.reference_method: Total Sn by ICP-MS; any quantifiable tin on a non-canned product triggers a packaging/contact-material investigation.

Cr-VI.control: Hexavalent chromium is a measurement artifact in a reducing food matrix: it reduces to Cr(III) in the presence of organic matter and gastric conditions, so a food does not carry a stable Cr(VI) burden. It is bounded by total chromium, which is measured on every lot; any total-Cr result at or above the reflex trigger prompts Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by EPA 3060A with IC-ICP-MS / EN 15192 or equivalent on a total-Cr exceedance.

MeHg.control: Methylmercury forms by microbial methylation in aquatic food chains and biomagnifies in fish; there is no methylmercury pathway in terrestrial cereal, pulse, or tuber crops. It is bounded by total mercury, which is measured on every lot.
MeHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS; reflex MeHg speciation (GC-ICP-MS) only on an elevated total-Hg result.

wet-meat-composite.analog_label: the animal-protein fraction of a complete diet — meat and meat products (adult/general human food, as consumed)

iAs.control: No government sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum for meat or meat products; total arsenic is measured on every lot and bounds the inorganic fraction, with speciation triggered on an elevated total-arsenic result.
iAs.reference_method: Total As by ICP-MS; inorganic As by HPLC-ICP-MS (EN 16802) on an elevated total-As result.

tAs.control: No government sets a total-arsenic maximum for general meat and meat products; total arsenic is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control and gates the inorganic-arsenic reflex.

tHg.control: Mercury does not biomagnify in terrestrial meat animals; no government sets a mercury maximum for general meat products. Total mercury is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control.
tHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS.

Ni.control: No government sets a nickel maximum for meat or meat products; total nickel is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control.

Cr.control: No government sets a total-chromium maximum for general meat products; total chromium is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control and gates the Cr(VI) reflex.

Al.control: No government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for general (non-infant) human foods; the only human-food aluminium numbers are permitted additive-residue limits, not contaminant maxima. Aluminium is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control.
Al.reference_method: Total Al by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion.

Sn.control: Tin is a can-migration analyte with no source in fresh, frozen, or refrigerated meat placed on market without a tin-coated container. Canned wet products are certified under the canned-wet tin read-across.
Sn.reference_method: Total Sn by ICP-MS; any quantifiable tin on a non-canned product triggers a packaging investigation.

Cr-VI.control: Hexavalent chromium reduces to Cr(III) in a reducing meat matrix and carries no stable burden; bounded by total chromium, measured on every lot. Any quantifiable Cr(VI) on a total-Cr exceedance fails certification.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by EPA 3060A with IC-ICP-MS / EN 15192 on a total-Cr exceedance.

MeHg.control: There is no methylmercury biomagnification pathway in terrestrial meat; bounded by total mercury, measured on every lot.
MeHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS; reflex MeHg speciation only on an elevated total-Hg result.

seafood-marine.analog_label: seafood — marine non-predatory finfish and forage fish sold for human consumption (as consumed)

Ni.control: No government sets a nickel maximum for finfish; total nickel is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control.

Cr.control: No government sets a total-chromium maximum for finfish; total chromium is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control and gates the Cr(VI) reflex.

Al.control: No government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for finfish or general human foods; the only human-food aluminium numbers are permitted additive-residue limits, not contaminant maxima. Aluminium is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control.
Al.reference_method: Total Al by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion.

Sn.control: Tin is a can-migration analyte; fresh, frozen, or refrigerated fish-based pet food has no tin source. Canned fish-based products are certified under the canned-wet tin read-across.
Sn.reference_method: Total Sn by ICP-MS; any quantifiable tin on a non-canned product triggers a packaging investigation.

Cr-VI.control: Hexavalent chromium reduces to Cr(III) in the fish matrix; bounded by total chromium, measured on every lot.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by EPA 3060A with IC-ICP-MS / EN 15192 on a total-Cr exceedance.

dairy-milk.analog_label: liquid milk and dairy products sold for human consumption (as consumed)

iAs.control: Dairy regulations set total-arsenic limits, not a separate inorganic-arsenic limit; total arsenic is measured on every lot and bounds the inorganic fraction, with speciation on an elevated total-arsenic result.
iAs.reference_method: Total As by ICP-MS; inorganic As by HPLC-ICP-MS (EN 16802) on an elevated total-As result.

Ni.analog_label: EU liquid infant/young-child formula nickel maximum
Ni.label: Human-grade read-across from the EU liquid milk-based formula nickel maximum (100 µg/kg, as consumed) where no general liquid-milk nickel maximum exists — the nearest human-food milk-matrix nickel limit.

Cr.analog_label: China GB 2762 total-chromium maximum for liquid milk
Cr.label: Human-grade read-across from China's GB 2762 total-chromium maximum for liquid milk (300 µg/kg, as consumed) — the nearest human-food milk-matrix total-chromium limit, and the value the human dairy standard adopts.

Al.label: Human-grade read-across from the AU-NZ non-soy milk-based formula aluminium maximum (500 µg/kg, as consumed) where no general liquid-milk aluminium maximum exists — the nearest human-food milk-matrix aluminium limit.

Sn.control: Tin is a packaging-migration analyte; non-tin-coated liquid milk replacers have no intrinsic tin pathway. A tin-coated pack is certified under the canned-wet tin read-across.
Sn.reference_method: Total Sn by ICP-MS; packaging declaration; any quantifiable tin triggers a packaging investigation.

Cr-VI.control: Hexavalent chromium reduces to Cr(III) in the milk matrix; bounded by total chromium, measured on every lot.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by EPA 3060A with IC-ICP-MS / EN 15192 on a total-Cr exceedance.

MeHg.control: There is no methylmercury bioaccumulation pathway in dairy; bounded by total mercury, measured on every lot.
MeHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS; reflex MeHg speciation only on an elevated total-Hg result.

Sn.analog_label: EU canned-food tin maximum (canned foods other than beverages)
Sn.label: Human-grade read-across from the strictest general canned-food tin maximum that matches the container (EU 200,000 µg/kg for canned foods other than beverages, as consumed). Tin is material for canned wet pet food because it migrates from the tin-coated can, exactly as for canned human food; the cured-meat non-tinplate tin limits are a different container class and are not applied to a tin-canned product.

pet-food-freeze-dried.name: Freeze-dried / dehydrated pet foods (including freeze-dried raw)

pet-milk-replacers-specialty-liquids.name: Milk replacers and specialty pet liquids
